Full marks may be obtained for answers to ALL questions. Mathematical formulae booklets published by the Board are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving the answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. Start each question on a fresh page.

questions.enonce_markdown: Find the range of values of $x$ for which $\dfrac{2x - 1}{x + 2} < -1$. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Do **not** multiply by $(x + 2)$ directly: its sign is unknown. Move everything to one side and combine into a single fraction ($x \neq -2$):
$$\frac{2x - 1}{x + 2} + 1 < 0 \;\Longrightarrow\; \frac{2x - 1 + x + 2}{x + 2} < 0 \;\Longrightarrow\; \frac{3x + 1}{x + 2} < 0.$$

The critical values are $x = -2$ (denominator zero, excluded) and $x = -\tfrac13$ (numerator zero).

| interval | $3x + 1$ | $x + 2$ | quotient |
|---|---|---|---|
| $x < -2$ | $-$ | $-$ | $+$ |
| $-2 < x < -\tfrac13$ | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ |
| $x > -\tfrac13$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |

The quotient is negative only for $-2 < x < -\tfrac13$:
$$\boxed{-2 < x < -\tfrac13}$$
(Check: $x = -1$ gives $\tfrac{-3}{1} = -3 < -1$ (true); $x = 0$ gives $-\tfrac12$ (false, not $< -1$); $x = -3$ gives $\tfrac{-7}{-1} = 7$ (false).)

questions.enonce_markdown: Find the range of values of $x$ for which $|2x - 4| < x + 1$. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Method 1 (squaring).** For the inequality to hold we need $x + 1 > 0$ (a modulus is never less than a negative number). With both sides non-negative, squaring preserves the inequality:
$$(2x - 4)^2 < (x + 1)^2 \;\Longrightarrow\; (2x - 4)^2 - (x + 1)^2 < 0 \;\Longrightarrow\; \left[(2x - 4) - (x + 1)\right]\left[(2x - 4) + (x + 1)\right] < 0$$
$$\Longrightarrow\; (x - 5)(3x - 3) < 0 \;\Longrightarrow\; 3(x - 5)(x - 1) < 0 \;\Longrightarrow\; 1 < x < 5.$$
This interval already satisfies $x > -1$.

**Method 2 (two-sided).** $|2x - 4| < x + 1 \iff -(x + 1) < 2x - 4 < x + 1$:
- right: $2x - 4 < x + 1 \Rightarrow x < 5$;
- left: $-x - 1 < 2x - 4 \Rightarrow 3 < 3x \Rightarrow x > 1$.

$$\boxed{1 < x < 5}$$
(Check: $x = 3$: $|2| = 2 < 4$ true; $x = 0.5$: $|-3| = 3 < 1.5$ false; $x = 6$: $8 < 7$ false.)

questions.enonce_markdown: The complex numbers $z_1$ and $z_2$ are such that $z_1 = -2 + 2i$ and $z_2 = -2 - 2i$. Find (a) $\arg z_1$; (b) $|z_2|^6$. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a)** $z_1 = -2 + 2i$ lies in the second quadrant of the Argand diagram (negative real part, positive imaginary part). The acute reference angle is $\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2}{2}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$, so
$$\arg z_1 = \pi - \frac{\pi}{4} = \boxed{\frac{3\pi}{4}} \quad(= 135^\circ),$$
taking the principal value $-\pi < \arg z \le \pi$.

**(b)** $|z_2| = \sqrt{(-2)^2 + (-2)^2} = \sqrt{8} = 2\sqrt2$. Then
$$|z_2|^6 = \left(2\sqrt2\right)^6 = 2^6 \cdot \left(\sqrt2\right)^6 = 64 \times 8 = \boxed{512}.$$
(Equivalently $|z_2|^6 = \left(|z_2|^2\right)^3 = 8^3 = 512$; this also equals $|z_2^6|$ since $|z^n| = |z|^n$.)
